content: GPR75, also known as Probable G-protein coupled receptor 75, is a protein encoded by the GPR75 gene in humans. It belongs to the family of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), which are cell surface receptors that initiate intracellular signaling cascades by activating guanine-nucleotide binding proteins (G proteins) upon ligand binding. Currently, GPR75 is classified as an orphan GPCR, meaning that its endogenous ligand has not yet been definitively identified. However, ongoing research is focused on determining its specific ligand and physiological roles. In one study, the chemokine CCL5, also known as RANTES, was found to stimulate calcium mobilization and the formation of inositol triphosphate in cells transfected with GPR75, suggesting a potential interaction. More recently, 20-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (20-HETE), a bioactive eicosanoid derived from the ω-hydroxylation of arachidonic acid, has been identified as a molecule that exerts its prohypertensive effects on the vasculature through the activation of GPR75-mediated Gq signaling pathways. This discovery was made by Dr. Schwartzman’s laboratory at New York Medical College, a leading research group in the field of 20-HETE biology. Their findings have provided significant new insights into the pharmacological and physiological roles of GPR75, particularly in the context of vascular function and hypertension.
